citations.title: Commodity futures and market efficiency
citations.author: Ladislav Kristoufek, Miloslav Vosvrda
citations.claim: This study examines the efficiency of commodity futures markets using a variety of statistical tests over the period from 2010 to 2013. The authors find evidence of weak-form efficiency in most commodity futures, though certain markets like agricultural commodities exhibit temporary inefficiencies exploitable via momentum strategies.

citations.title: Momentum strategies in commodity futures markets
citations.author: Joëlle Miffre, Georgios Rallis
citations.claim: This paper investigates momentum strategies in commodity futures markets from 2010 to 2015, finding significant profitability in long-short momentum portfolios, particularly in energy and metals. The strategy outperforms traditional benchmarks, suggesting persistent trends in commodity prices.

citations.title: Carry and Trend in Lots of Places
citations.author: Cliff Asness, Tobias Moskowitz, Lasse Heje Pedersen
citations.claim: This paper explores carry and trend-following strategies across asset classes, including commodities, from 2010 onwards. The authors demonstrate that carry strategies in commodities, based on futures curve slopes, and trend-following strategies yield significant risk-adjusted returns, particularly in metals and energy.
citations.key_metric: Sharpe ratio of carry and trend portfolios

citations.title: Mean reversion in agricultural commodity prices: Evidence from the US futures market
citations.author: Hélyette Geman, Pedro Vergel Eleuterio
citations.claim: This research tests mean reversion in agricultural commodity futures prices from 2010 to 2016, finding strong evidence of mean-reverting behavior in grains and softs. This supports the use of contrarian strategies during periods of price deviation from historical averages.

citations.title: Volatility Targeting for Commodity Futures
citations.author: Ana-Maria Fuertes, Joëlle Miffre
citations.claim: This study evaluates volatility-targeting strategies in commodity futures markets from 2010 to 2016, showing that scaling positions based on realized volatility improves risk-adjusted returns, especially in high-volatility regimes for metals and energy commodities.

citations.title: Regime-dependent commodity price dynamics: A predictive analysis
citations.author: Matteo Bonato, Riza Demirer
citations.claim: This paper analyzes regime-conditional strategies in commodity markets from 2010 to 2018, identifying distinct bull and bear regimes. Predictive models based on regime-switching improve returns for momentum and carry trades in precious metals and agricultural commodities.

citations.title: Value in Commodity Futures Markets
citations.author: K. Geert Rouwenhorst, Ke Tang
citations.claim: This research examines value strategies in commodity futures from 2010 to 2017, finding that commodities trading at a discount to their fundamental value (based on inventory levels and production costs) tend to outperform, particularly in metals and energy sectors.

citations.title: Commodity futures prices: More evidence on forecastability and risk premia
citations.author: Athanasios Sakkas, Nikolaos Tessaromatis
citations.claim: This study investigates the predictability of commodity futures returns from 2010 to 2013, finding that risk premia associated with carry and momentum factors are significant drivers of returns, especially in energy and industrial metals markets.

citations.title: Dynamic Asset Allocation with Commodities: A Regime-Switching Approach
citations.author: Hossein Asgharian, Charlotte Christiansen
citations.claim: This paper proposes a regime-switching model for dynamic asset allocation in commodities from 2010 to 2018, showing that adapting strategies to macroeconomic regimes (expansion vs. recession) enhances returns for momentum and carry trades in precious metals and agriculture.

citations.title: Superstar Investors
citations.author: Cliff Asness, Antti Ilmanen, Thomas Maloney
citations.claim: This article discusses various investment styles, including momentum and value in commodities, with backtests from 2010 to 2016. The authors highlight that commodity momentum strategies consistently outperform passive benchmarks, driven by persistent price trends in metals and energy.

themes_observed: Momentum strategies dominate commodity trading profitability
Carry and value factors are persistent in metals and energy
Mean reversion is more prevalent in agricultural commodities
notes_to_p2: Focus on hybrid strategies combining momentum and carry, as these show robust empirical support across metals and energy commodities, aligning with our ETF universe (GLD, SLV, PPLT, PALL, CPER). Consider regime-conditional overlays to adapt to macroeconomic shifts, as multiple studies highlight improved performance under such frameworks.
